Read the initial-state distribution of a fit

Source: R/tidy-accessors.R
initial.Rd

initial() returns the initial-state distribution of a fit, one row per state: the proportion of sequences that begin in each state. It describes how episodes open, which the transition table cannot show, and it completes the description of the process as a first-order Markov chain together with transition_probabilities().

A fit built from a transition-count matrix has no sequences and so no initial states; the table then has no rows.

Usage

initial(fit)

# S3 method for class 'lsa'
initial(fit)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_group'
initial(fit)

Arguments

fit

An lsa fit from lsa(), or a grouped fit from lsa(..., group = ).

Value

A data.frame with one row per state and the columns state and init_prob (summing to 1). A grouped fit gains a leading group column.

See also

transition_probabilities(), nodes(), transitions()

Examples

initial(lsa(engagement))
#>        state init_prob
#> 1     Active 0.3823529
#> 2    Average 0.3676471
#> 3 Disengaged 0.2500000
